regional.syndrome: Sudden high fever with severe, often symmetrical polyarthralgia and rash; the name means 'that which bends up'. Arthritis persists for months to years in 30–40%. regional.headline: Alphavirus of the Semliki Forest complex causing explosive epidemics of febrile polyarthritis.
regional.prevention: Vector control; the virus-like particle vaccine Vimkunya is licensed from 12 years of age. regional.geography: Africa, Asia, Indian Ocean, Americas since 2013, with autochthonous outbreaks in southern Europe.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.incubation: Decades. Myelopathy appears after years; leukaemia typically forty to sixty years after perinatal infection.
regional.syndrome: Lifelong asymptomatic carriage in over 90%. Adult T-cell leukaemia/lymphoma (ATL) appears after a latency of forty to sixty years, usually in those infected through breastfeeding, with a lifetime risk of a few per cent; HTLV-1-associated myelopathy/tropical spastic paraparesis (HAM/TSP) in under 4%, presenting as spastic paraparesis with bladder dysfunction. regional.geography: Sharply defined endemic foci rather than a global distribution: south-western Japan, the Caribbean, parts of South America, West and Central Africa, Iran, Romania, and Aboriginal communities of central Australia, where some adult seroprevalences exceed 40%.

regional.syndrome: Dengue fever: high fever, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia/arthralgia ('breakbone fever'), rash.
